sentences.text: The case of the applicant is that a complaint was lodged by the opposite party No. 2 on 09.10.2024 against the applicant under Section 23 read with Section 20 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 with an allegation that the opposite party no. 2 has been dispossessed by the applicant from her matrimonial house and the applicant has stopped giving the opposite party No. 2 money to maintain herself.

sentences.text:
Thus, it was prayed that the complainant/ opposite party No. 2, wife be provided Rs. 12,000/- per month as society charges from the respondent, Rs.
5,000/- per month be recovered from the respondent as electricity dues, Rs. 50,000/- per month for household expenses and Rs. 35,000/- per month for food, clothing, medical treatment and other needs and damage to the tune of Rs. 20,00,000/- and Rs. 1,00,000/- be provided to the complainant, opposite party no. 2 as interim compensation.

Final prayer was made to the court below to pass an order in favour of the complainant/ opposite party No. 2 for grant of Rs.
1,00,000/- per month as interim compensation from the respondent on the said proceedings.
On the said proceedings, notices have been issued to the applicant.

5. Questioning the complaint as well as the impugned notice dated 04.02.2025 passed by the learned Civil Judge (Junior Division), F.T.C.-II, Gautam Buddh Nagar through District Probationary Officer, District Gautam Budh Nagar in Case No. 692 of 2024, under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, the present application has been preferred.

Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that complaint so sought to be lodged by the opposite party No. 2 is not maintainable for the simple reason that the marriage of the opposite party No. 2 stood solemnized with applicant on 22.10.2023 and proceedings under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act stood initiated by the applicant which culminated into passing of an order by the Principal Judge, Family Court, Bulandshahar in Criminal Case No. 1181 of 2024 on 28.10.2024 whereby exparte the proceedings came to be allowed in favour of the applicant and marriage was declared void.

Submission is that though First Appeal (Defective) No. 482 of 2025 has been preferred by the opposite party No. 2 being Ms. Nidhi Chaudhary @ Nidhi Mallick v. Shri Vikash Chaudhary which is pending before this Court but the order declaring the marriage as null and void is with intact.

sentences.text: 7. In nutshell, the submission is that once the opposite party No. 2 is not having any domestic relationship with the applicant and there happens to be a decree of a Court then the opposite party No. 2 does not answer the description of an 'aggrieved person' under Section 2(a) of the Act.

There is no domestic relationship as per the Section 2(f) of the Act if the applicant cannot be termed as respondent under Section 2(q) of the Act and there is no share household under Section 2(s) of the Act.
8.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that the applicant has been subjected to harassment at all levels, particularly, when the marriage of the opposite party No. 2 was solemnized with one Manish Ahuja on 18.09.1999 and from their wedlock, one daughter was born.

Later on, a divorce petition came to be preferred bearing No. 75 of 2013, under Section 13A of the Hindu Marriage Act before the concerned Family Court which is pending consideration and thereafter another divorce petition came to be preferred under Section 13A being Divorce Petition No. 512 of 2013 before the court of Tis Hazari, Delhi and another petition under Section 13A of the Hindu Vikas Chaudhary vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: It is also contended that another Divorce Petition No. 1372 of 2023, under Section 13-A of the Act is also pending before the Court of Tis Hazari, Delhi.
Submission is that ultimately, the marriage of the opposite party no. 2 with Manish Ahuja came to be dissolved by order dated 05.07.2023 in subsequent Divorce Petition No. 1942 of 2023.

It is also contended that the opposite party No. 2 solemnized second marriage with one Naru Gopal Singh S/o late Anil Singh and later on, the opposite party No. 2 lodged a first information report against Naru Gopal Singh being FIR No. 217 of 2014, under Sections 376, 417, 313, 354, 323,
120B, IPC in police station Patuli, District Kolkata and further another FIR No. 48 of 2014, under Section 66, 66A of I.T. Act read with Section 506 IPC was also lodged in police station Patuli,
District Kolkata.
It is further contended that Naru Gopal Singh was enlarged on bail and opposite party No. 2 filed a bail cancellation application.
The opposite party No.2 also preferred criminal miscellaneous transfer application to transfer the proceedings.
9. Contention of the learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant is a divorcee whose marriage was dissolved with another woman on 01.11.2022 under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act.

However, the opposite party No. 2 without disclosing her identity and antecedents become intimate with the applicant through a website, Shaadi.com and the opposite party No. 2 took huge amount through UPI, though she refunded negligible amount and huge amount is with her and she lodged a first information report being FIR No. 0475 of 2023, under Sections 376, 307,
504 IPC, Police Station Beeta-2, District Gautam Budh Nagar.

condition

was imposed by the opposite party No. 2 forcing the applicant to get married and on the said basis, the applicant was enlarged on bail on 09.10.2023 and on 22.10.2023, marriage was solemnized of the applicant with the opposite party no. 2 in Arya Samaj Temple in NOIDA and it was also registered.

10. Submission of the learned counsel for the applicant is that the opposite party No. 2 is habitual in harassing the applicant and she, without disclosing her antecedents, is just harassing the applicant just for money.

Further submission is that a first information report was also lodged by the opposite party No. 2 against the applicant under Section 85, 316(2), 115(2), 352 and 126 of the BNS in FIR No. 0065 of 2025 and the applicant preferred Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 6640 of 2025 (Vikas Chaudhary v. State of U.P. and 3 others) in which the applicant was accorded interim protection.

sentences.text: 11. Thus, the submission of the learned counsel for the applicant is that the present proceedings is nothing but the grossest misuse of process of law, particularly, when the opposite party No. 2 is taking recourse to variety of reliefs as provided under different enactments.

He submits that once the marriage of the applicant with the opposite party No. 2 stands annulled then there is no relationship between them so as to give to a tool to the opposite party no. 2 to misuse the provisions of Domestic Violence Act.
It is, thus, prayed that the complaint as well as the order issuing notice by the court below be set aside.

12. Learned AGA as well as counsel appearing for the opposite party No. 2 while countering the submissions so made by the counsel for the applicant has submitted that this Court may not be interfered at this stage, particularly, when complaint has been filed and notices have been issued.

According to them, merely because the opposite party No. 2,
marriage has been annulled, would not be a ground to be forestall the claim of the opposite party No. 2, particularly, the words employed under Section 2(a) defining aggrieved person means any woman who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the respondent and who alleges to have been subjected to any act of domestic violence by the respondent.
Further submission is that domestic relationship is not restricted to two persons who are living but it stands applied to two persons who at any point of time have lived.

13. Reliance has been placed upon the decision in Application U/S 482 No. 12826 of 2023 (Shashank Pandey and 2 others v. State of U.P. and another), decided on 20.02.2024 and Application 528 BNSS No. 11345 of 2025 (Ram Kumar Pandey v. State of U.P. and another), decided on 27.05.2025.

sentences.text: It is further contended that against the exparte order, annulling the marriage, a First Appeal (Defective) No. 482 of 2025 is already pending.
14. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the records carefully.
15. Apparently, the marriage of the applicant stood solemnized with the opposite party No. 2 on 22.10.2023.

The proceedings under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act was instituted by the applicant on 02.09.2024 before the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Bulandshahr in Matrimonial Case No. 1181 of 2024 which came to be decreed on 28.10.2024 annulling the marriage.

entities.text: Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Bulandshahr
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The allegations in the complaint are relatable to dispossessing the opposite party No. 2 on 28.03.2024 by the applicant.

The question as to whether the opposite party no. 2, wife is an aggrieved person or not as per Section 2(a) of the Act depends upon the facts and circumstances and the allegations set out in the complaint.

Pertinently, the words 'aggrieved person' has been defined as a woman who is or has been in domestic relationship with the respondent and who alleges to have been subjected to any act of domestic relationship by the respondent.

More so Section 2(f) deals with domestic relationship which means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity,
marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or are family members living together as a joint family.

So much so, Section 2(q) defines respondent means any adult male person who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the aggrieved person and against whom the aggrieved person has sought any relief under this Act; and Section 2(s) of the Act defines shared household means a household where the person aggrieved lives or at any stage has lived in a domestic relationship either singly or along with the respondent.

16. Looking into the nature of the allegations sought to be levelled in the complaint as well as the documents available on record, prime facie, it is apparent that the applicant and opposite party No.
2 were husband and wife.
The question as to whether rightly or wrongly, their marriage stood dissolved is a question which is sub-judice before the Court of law.
Thus no findings can be recorded therein.

More so what would be relevant, would be the use of the word "at any point of time", thus,
the question as to whether any domestic violence was suffered by the opposite party No. 2 is a question of trial in the proceedings.

sentences.text:
In Shashank Pandey and 2 others (supra), a co-ordinate Bench of this Court observed as under:
"25. In Amit Agarwal v. Sanjay Aggarwal, (2016) SCC OnLine P&H 4200

entities.text: Amit Agarwal v. Sanjay Aggarwal, (2016) SCC OnLine P&H 4200
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , a Single Judge Bench of Punjab and Haryana High Court held that answer to the question whether aggrieved person would even mean a 'divorced woman', lies in the definition provided in Section 2(a), which says that "aggrieved person" means any woman who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the respondent and who alleges to have been subjected to any act of domestic violence by the respondent".
The Punjab and Haryana High Court held that: -
"19. The use of the word is any woman 'who is' or 'has been'.
Both the expressions are in the present tense.
The legislature has not used the word 'who was' or 'had been'.
This means the domestic relationship has to be in the present and not in the past.

The definition requires that on the date Act come into force, the woman should be in domestic relationship."
30.

The applicant does not dispute that he got married to the opposite party no. 2 and having been married to the applicant, the opposite party no. 2 had lived in a domestic relationship with the applicant, before they started living separately.
They had been related by marriage till the marriage was declared to be null and void.

Even though the marriage has subsequently been declared to be null and void, when the relationship between the applicant and the opposite party no. 2 subsisted, it was a relationship in the nature of marriage.
Therefore, the opposite party no. 2 is an aggrieved person within the meaning of the Act she has a right to present an application under Section 12 of the DV Act."
18. Nonetheless in the present proceedings at this stage, this Court is not required to adjudge the merits of the allegations as they are the subject matter of proceedings.
What is required, is that the allegations should not be such which makes the entire claim frivolous.
19. Looking into the nature of the relief sought in the complaint as well as the status of the opposite party No. 2, this Court does not find any justification to interfere.

Even otherwise, the allegations so made by the rival parties upon the conduct of each other, is not liable to be considered at this stage in the present proceedings, particularly, when the question of consideration, if any, would arise when the proceedings are allowed to be continued.
Any observation of this Court in this regard is not required at all.

20. Recently the Hon'ble Apex Court had the occasion to consider the extent of judicial intervention in the matters where the complaint under Section 12 of the D.V. Act are challenged in the proceedings under Section 482 Cr.P.C./ 528 BNSS in Criminal Appeal No. 2688 of 2025 (Shaurabh Kumar Tripathi Vs. Vidhi Rawal) decided on 19.05.2025, the following was observed.-

entities.text: Shaurabh Kumar Tripathi Vs. Vidhi Rawal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
When it comes to exercise of power under Section 482 of the CrPC in relation to application under Section 12(1), the High Court has to keep in mind the fact that the DV Act, 2005 is a welfare legislation specially enacted to give justice to those Vikas Chaudhary vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178196493/
5 women who suffer from domestic violence and for preventing acts of domestic violence.

entities.text: Vikas Chaudhary vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, while exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 of the CrPC for quashing proceedings under Section 12(1), the High Court should be very slow and circumspect.
Interference can be made only when the case is clearly of gross illegality or gross abuse of the process of law.
Generally, the High Court must adopt a hands-off approach while dealing with proceedings under Section 482 for quashing an application under Section 12(1).

Unless the High Courts show restraint in the exercise of jurisdiction under Section 482 of the CrPC while dealing with a prayer for quashing the proceedings under the DV Act, 2005, the very object of enacting the DV Act, 2005, will be defeated.

39. To conclude, the view taken in the impugned order of the High Court that a petition under Section 482 of the CrPC for challenging the proceedings emanating from Section 12(1) of the DV Act, 2005 is not maintainable, is not the correct view.

We hold that High Courts can exercise power under Section 482 of CrPC (Section 528 of the BNSS) for quashing the proceedings emanating from the application under Section 12(1) of the DV Act, 2005, pending before the Court of the learned Magistrate.
However, considering the object of the DV Act, 2005, the High Courts should exercise caution and circumspection when dealing with an application under Section 12(1).
Normally, interference under Section 482 is warranted only in the case of gross illegality or injustice."

21. Cumulatively analyzing the case from the four corners of law, this Court does not find the present case to come within the exceptional category for interference, particularly, in the present proceedings, only notices have been issued to the applicant.

Thus, interference is declined,
accordingly, the application stands disposed of granting liberty to the applicant to contest the matter and to raise all legal and factual issues or grounds which are legally permissible under law and this Court has no reason to disbelieve then the same shall be considered in correct perspective.
